summary: The English of 6:7-6:11 is faithful and keeps the sayings and proof texts plain; its few faults are a plural for the singular קִנְיָנֶךָ (Ps 104:24), a feminine reading of the pausal masculine לָךְ (Prov 3:2), a wrong 'verbal noun' note on וַהֲקִיצוֹתָ and a wrong binyan for לְזַכּוֹת. The senses were filled mechanically: most are sense 1, often of the wrong homograph (proper names such as Rosh, Anak, Atarah, Jamin, Adam, Tob, Kanah, Shem for the common words; 'gnat' for כֵּן, 'menstruation' for עַד), or a label ('adj', 'n f', 'peh'), or the Qal sense for a Niphal; these are re-pointed to the right entry or removed with a note. The apparatus collapsed major Vilna variants (two missing proof texts in 6:7, a different attribution and verse order in 6:8, לפי in 6:9, the half-verse and אדני in 6:10). The model morphology needed fixes to state (suffixed nouns, צְבָאוֹת, שֶׁבַע, רֵאשִׁית, מִקְּדָשׁ), number (duals), segmentation (מִשּׁוּם, מֵאָז, כֻּלָּם), binyan (בָּרוּךְ is Qal passive), pausal 2ms suffixes, and several roots and lemmas.

patches.value: Rabbi Yose son of Kisma said: Once I was walking on the road and a certain man met me, and he greeted me, and I returned his greeting. He said to me: Rabbi, from what place are you? I said to him: I am from a great city of sages and of scribes. He said to me: Rabbi, is it your wish to dwell with us in our place? And I will give you a thousand thousand dinars of gold and precious stones and pearls. I said to him: My son, if you give me all the silver and gold and precious stones and pearls that are in the world, I dwell nowhere except in a place of Torah. And not only that, but at the hour of a person's departure nothing accompanies a person: neither silver nor gold nor precious stones or pearls, but only Torah and good deeds, as it is said: When you walk, it will lead you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and when you awake, it will talk with you. When you walk, it will lead you in this world; when you lie down, it will watch over you in the grave; and when you awake, it will talk with you in the world to come. And so it is written in the Book of Psalms by the hand of David, king of Israel: The Torah of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver. And it says: Mine is the silver and mine is the gold, says the LORD of hosts.
patches.reason: 'as it is said' continued the sentence but began after a full stop in lower case; joined to the sentence it proves.

patches.value: Five possessions the Holy One, blessed be He, acquired for Himself in His world, and these are they: Torah, one possession; heaven and earth, one possession; Abraham, one possession; Israel, one possession; the Temple, one possession. Torah: from where do we know it? For it is written: The LORD acquired me as the beginning of His way, before His works of old. Heaven and earth, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: Thus says the LORD: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool; what house is it that you would build for Me and what is the place of My rest? And it says: How many are Your works, O LORD; You made them all in wisdom; the earth is full of Your possession. Abraham, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: And he blessed him and said: Blessed be Abram to God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth. Israel, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: Until Your people pass over, O LORD, until the people You acquired pass over. And it says: As for the holy ones who are in the land, they, and the majestic ones, all my delight is in them. The Temple, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: The place for Your dwelling You made, O LORD; the sanctuary, O LORD, Your hands established. And it says: And He brought them to the border of His holiness, this mountain that His right hand acquired.
patches.reason: קִנְיָנֶךָ (Ps 104:24) is singular, and the mishnah cites it for one קִנְיָן: 'Your possession', not 'Your possessions'. Also: a colon before each quoted verse, and 'My throne' capitalized like 'My footstool'.
